problem: Foundation visual navigation models (GNM/ViNT/NoMaD) use RGB only and are trained on collision-free data, so they collide in narrow, structured indoor spaces. Point-goal approaches also accumulate odometry error over long horizons.
motivation: Indoor environments have dense structures and narrow corridors, where a collision causes damage or gets the robot stuck and ends the episode. Depth is tied directly to geometry and gives better obstacle cues, and a compact model trained on little data allows fast on-board inference.
key_idea: A lightweight GRU-based action predictor uses depth and pose history to output collision-aware waypoints and a corrected sub-goal pose. A depth collision predictor triggers propagation of the correction offset to all future sub-goals in the topological map.
insight: Collision-aware waypoints alone only avoid immediate obstacles. Without sub-goal pose correction the robot keeps aiming at an odometry-drifted sub-goal and eventually collides. In the ablation, DevGRU-Base scores NC 0.82 / SPL 0.25, No-SG-Correction scores 0.73 / 0.49, and Full scores 0.99 / 0.73. Collision data and pose correction are therefore complementary, and a small GRU on depth suffices for strong real-robot performance.
method: Topological navigation: a precomputed graph of nodes (pose, depth image) from teleoperation. Sub-goal poses are estimated from odometry during navigation and a sub-goal counts as reached once the robot is within a threshold of the corrected pose.

Action Predictor (AP): EfficientNet-B0 encodes each of N=6 depth frames and an MLP encodes each pose. A goal token comes from the concatenated current and sub-goal depth plus the sub-goal pose. A GRU processes the tokens and heads predict K=5 future waypoints and the corrected sub-goal pose.
AP loss: L = α·L_wp + (1-α)·L_sg with α=0.5. L_sg is a Smooth L1 position term plus a quaternion orientation term. L_wp is an MSE position term plus a quaternion orientation term.
Collision Predictor (CP): an EfficientNet depth binary classifier outputs a collision probability from a single depth image.
SG pose correction: when p_col is high, the offset Δp = p̂_i ⊖ p̃_i is applied to all future sub-goal poses.

Collision data collection: DevGRU-Base is deployed without the CP step, a human records the collisions, and collision-free waypoints and sub-goal poses are recomputed with cubic Hermite splines and curvature-adaptive sampling. This gives about 10K collision samples plus about 10K collision-free samples.
Control: the predicted waypoints are fed to a position controller on a real wheeled robot with a RealSense D435 depth camera.

setting.backbone: EfficientNet-B0 + GRU action predictor (14.77M) and EfficientNet collision predictor (4.66M), trained from scratch/ImageNet-style encoder
setting.training_data: Own dataset of about 10K collision-free teleoperated samples from 5 campus buildings plus about 10K collision samples generated by re-running DevGRU-Base; no foundation model distillation
setting.observation: depth images (6-frame history) + odometry poses; sub-goal depth image and pose
setting.action_space: predicted waypoints (5 future poses) fed to a position controller
setting.privileged: none online; a topological map with sub-goal depth images and poses is precomputed by manual teleoperation, and 2D lidar is used only for post-analysis

numbers_note: Custom real-robot benchmark, so none of the canonical benchmarks apply. NC is the paper's own node-coverage metric. Per-scene numbers are in Table 1 and are not all listed here.
results: DevGRU averages NC 0.89 and SPL 0.80 across 9 real-world scenes, beating NavDP (0.82 / 0.60) and far ahead of ViNT (0.62 / 0.15), NoMaD (0.3 / 0) and the fine-tuned variants (SPL ≤0.11). It has 19.44M parameters and 50.01 ms mean inference, versus NavDP's 135.72M and 860.18 ms, and NoMaD's 123.46 ms and ViNT's 176.57 ms.
limitations: Evaluation is small: 9 scenes with 2 runs each, one robot, and a custom NC metric, so it has no standard benchmark or statistical comparison.
It needs a manually precomputed topological map and additional real-robot collision data collection, and it relies on odometry-based pose estimates.
DevGRU does not win every scene (for example T-B8 with NC 0.69 / SPL 0.46, against ViNT's 1 / 0.92), and the baselines use different modalities and goal specifications, which complicates comparison.
